question: If m and n are positive integers and (m – n) is an even number, then (m² – n²) will always be divisible by:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

m − n even ⇒ m and n have same parity (both even or both odd)

Then m + n is also even

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

Even × Even = divisible by 4

**∴ Answer = 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

m − n is even

**Formula used:**

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

**Calculation:**

⇒ If m − n is even ⇒ m and n are both even or both odd

⇒ Case 1: m, n both even ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ Case 2: m, n both odd ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ So in all cases, both factors are even

⇒ Product = even × even

⇒ Hence divisible by 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

Parity Concept

Same parity numbers give even sum and difference.

Divisibility Rule

Product of two even numbers is always divisible by 4.
